title: sutra_winnow — multi-axis composite query
description:
Single MCP tool that AND-intersects existing signals (kind, complexity, churn, calls_to, calls_from, file glob, name regex, PageRank importance) with per-axis operators (`gt`, `in`, `matches`, `contains`).

Today an agent answering "functions calling `db::exec`, complexity > 10, churned in last 30d, ranked by PageRank" makes 4 calls and merges by hand. This collapses it to one round trip.

Each axis already exists as its own tool — implementation is intersect + rank.

See docs/feature-ideas.md → "sutra_winnow".

**Independent of other simple-additions tasks** — new tool, no shared response-builder edits.

acceptance_criteria.text: sutra_winnow accepts at least: kind, complexity, churn, calls_to, file_glob, name_regex, rank_by axes
Returns symbols matching all constraints AND-intersected
Each result includes the per-axis values that qualified it (importance, complexity, churn) so agents can explain the result

decisions: calls_to requires analysis tier (uses refs table) — guarded at MCP layer
Churn computed lazily only when min_churn or rank_by=churn is specified
Per-entry freshness included by default (consistent with task 1)
WinnowFilter struct keeps tool handler testable without MCP overhead
